title: Proactive latency fence and autotune surge mitigator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Automate batching/caching recommendations while guaranteeing latency/throughput SLOs using a lightweight guardrail layer: cohort token-bucket limiters, p95/p99 EWMA fences, SLO-aware routing decisions, and anomaly detectors that trigger staged rollback. The feature should produce actionable config suggestions and apply them through a safe staged pipeline (shadow -> canary -> phased) with automatic rollback if SLOs degrade beyond configured thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) System exposes automated config suggestions for batching and KV cache profiles per traffic cohort (JSON output + human-readable rationale).

2) New guardrail layer enforces per-cohort token-bucket limiters and an EWMA-based latency fence evaluating inference.latency.p95 and p99, preventing autotune changes from increasing SLO breach rate above configurable tolerance.

3) SLO-aware router can route traffic to fallback model variants or lower-batch profiles when a cohort's latency fence trips, with <50ms decision latency added to request path (measured at 99th percentile).

4) Anomaly detection (rolling-window robust z-score over latency and queue_length metrics) identifies regressions within 5 minutes and initiates an automated staged rollback policy (shadow -> canary -> full), documented in runbook.

5) End-to-end e2e test harness (simulated traffic with mixed sequence lengths) validates safe rollback triggers and records metrics to the console dashboard; tests pass in CI with synthetic replay scenarios.
6) Dashboard surfaces per-cohort cost delta, latency impact, and rollback events with links to PRs and config diffs.
7) No customer-facing incidents during canary rollouts in internal dogfood over a 2-week burn-in period.
8) Changes are backward-compatible with existing routing policies and support manual override by operators in Console.
9) Implementation includes a minimal audit trail (who applied config, reason, links) for Private deployments.
10) Performance overhead introduced by the guardrail layer is <2% p50 latency and <5% p99 latency on average in lab runs compared to baseline.
design_decisions: Use EWMA (alpha=0.2) over p95 and p99 latency metrics to create fast-reacting but smooth fences — aggressive enough to catch regressions but resilient to single outliers.
Per-cohort token-bucket limiters keyed by model + route + customer_tier to prevent noisy tenants from destabilizing batching optimizations.
Anomaly detector based on robust z-score using median and MAD over a 30-minute sliding window; alerts at z>5 for p99 and z>3 for queue_length.
SLO-aware routing scores combine normalized latency headroom, recent error-rate delta, and a cost-savings signal — routing decision thresholds are configurable via Console.

Apply configs through a 3-phase pipeline: shadow (0% effect, telemetry only) -> canary (1-5% traffic, 30m observation) -> phased (25%, 60m -> 100%). Automatic rollback if fence breaches occur during canary or phased stages.
Shadow experiments are mandatory for all new batching/caching recommendations for 24 hours before canary unless explicitly bypassed with documented justification.
Keep the guardrail implementation as a thin sidecar service that subscribes to runtime metrics and publishes decisions to the control plane; avoids adding latency to the hot path.
Audit logs stored in structured JSON events written to the same audit pipeline used by Private deployments (KMS-wrapped where configured).
Expose config suggestions via SDK endpoint and Console UI with a diff/preview and a one-click staged apply + rollback button.
Fail-open vs fail-closed: in the rare case guardrail service is unavailable, default to safe conservative batching profile (fail-safe) and notify operators.
Metrics names standardized: inference.latency.p50/p95/p99, inference.throughput.tokens_per_sec, queue.length, config.suggested_savings_pct, guardrail.fence_tripped_count.
Keep fallback model variants pre-warmed in Dedicated pools to avoid cold-start latency when routing occurs.
Prioritize rollout for hosted tenants first, then Dedicated, then Private (due to different audit/KMS constraints).
implementation_notes: Backend: implement guardrail sidecar in Go, use existing telemetry ingestion (Prometheus/OTel) for streaming metrics and compute EWMA in-memory per cohort.
Persist decisions and audit events to Postgres events table (schema defined in runtime-migrations/2025-02-guardrails.sql).
Router changes: extend routing policy to accept guardrail advice token; add fallback path selection logic and route tagging for telemetry.
Config apply pipeline: reuse rollout engine with new staged plan type 'optimize-autotune' and add automatic triggers for rollback based on fence events.
CI: add synthetic replay tests (100k requests) with mixed seq lengths to validate p99 behavior under load; new test suite in runtime-tests/guardrail-suite.
Console: add 'Optimization' tab under model routes showing suggestions, canary progress, and rollback controls. Work with design for UX copy and warnings.
Security: ensure audit events include user_id and team_id; integrate with SSO for apply approvals when applied to Private deployments.
Telemetry: add high-cardinality labels sparingly (cohort_id, model_id, route) and pre-aggregate by cohort to avoid cardinality explosion.
Performance target: guardrail CPU usage must be <5% on smallest control-plane instance type used in Dedicated customers.
Create a preflight check that verifies required metrics for a cohort exist (min 1 hour history) before allowing canary apply.
Provide a CLI tool (rwctl) command `rwctl guardrail apply --preview` producing a JSON diff and simulation of expected latency impact.
Add feature flag `guardrail.autotune.v1` to gate rollout and allow emergency disable.
Document runbook for manual rollback including Grafana dashboard panels and Prometheus alerts to watch.
Coordinate with Solutions Eng to run two enterprise customers in closed beta for 3 weeks and collect feedback.
Estimate integration work with Dedicated autoscaler team ~2 weeks for pre-warming fallback variants (ENG-77201).
metrics: Primary SLOs: inference.latency.p95 < 180ms for web-tier routes, inference.latency.p99 < 500ms (configurable per route).
Safety thresholds: increase in p99 > 15% within 10m OR sustained p95 breach rate > 0.5% triggers immediate rollback in canary phase.
Anomaly windows: 5m alerting for rapid regressions, 30m evaluation window for automated policy decisions.
Observability: add dashboard panels for per-cohort EWMA latency, queue_length histogram, and cost delta heatmap.
Logs: include event-level context (cohort_id, suggested_profile_id, before/after tokenization window, applying_user, correlation_id).
SLO-aware routing score components: latency_headroom_score, error_trend_score, cost_savings_score (all normalized 0-100).
rollouts_and_rollback_policy: Phases: Shadow (telemetry only, min 24h) -> Canary (1-5% traffic, 30m observe) -> Phased (25% for 60m -> 100%).
Automatic rollback triggers: any Canery/Phased fence_tripped_count > 0 AND p99 uplift > 10% -> immediate rollback to previous stable config.
Manual rollback: operator can trigger via Console; rollback must create an audit event and optionally open an incident ticket template.
Post-rollback actions: run differential telemetry comparison, capture heap of recent traces, and create follow-up task to investigate root cause.
Escalations: after auto-rollback, page on-call SRE and notify product owner if customer_impact != none.
Safety net: if guardrail service itself fails during rollout, apply conservative fallback profile and mark rollout as failed.
Shadow-run expiry: suggestions that do not move to canary within 7 days are archived and require re-evaluation.
Operators can pin specific cohorts to 'no-optimize' to opt out of automated suggestions.
Record time-to-rollback metric and target median < 3 minutes for automatic rollback actions.
Runbook: include step-by-step for diagnosing fence trips, extracting traces, and re-running suggested profile in a controlled replay.
Compliance: all rollback actions in Private must be accompanied by an approval ticket or emergency flag as per enterprise policy.
